gen_risks.description: Procurement delays, weak contract management, and limited market competition in fragile and conflict-affected settings may impede the timely acquisition of laboratory equipment, medical supplies, and civil works.
gen_risks.mitigation: Hire experienced procurement specialists, adopt flexible and fit-for-purpose procurement arrangements in FCV areas, conduct early market engagement, and track transactions in STEP.
gen_risks.evidence: Procurement Risks include delays, governance issues, weak contract management, and limited market competition in fragile settings.

gen_risks.description: Challenging macro-fiscal outlooks, high public debt burdens, and volatile commodity revenues across participating countries risk underfunding routine health operations and threatening long-term financial sustainability.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide technical assistance to integrate health security into national Medium-Term Expenditure Frameworks, establish budget expenditure tracking, and explore public-private partnerships.
gen_risks.evidence: A challenging macro-fiscal outlook and high poverty levels make the region particularly vulnerable to shocks...

gen_risks.description: Project activities executed in remote regions or by decentralized implementation partners carry financial management risks of ineligible or undocumented expenditures.
gen_risks.mitigation: Disseminate adapted financial management procedural manuals to local partners, conduct quarterly risk-based internal audits, and enforce annual external audits.
gen_risks.evidence: several activities under the project like workshops, trainings and the local-level capacity building are at risk to generate questionable expenditures in Cameroon.

gen_risks.description: Administrative inefficiencies and delays in fulfilling post-effectiveness legal covenants (e.g., PIU staffing and accounting software customization) could postpone project implementation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Utilize Project Preparation Advances to initiate early recruitment, closely monitor covenant compliance timelines, and provide targeted World Bank implementation support.
gen_risks.evidence: Political and administrative inefficiencies could slow project execution.

gen_risks.description: Inadequate stakeholder engagement and communication could lead to the exclusion of vulnerable or marginalized populations—such as IDPs, refugees, rural women, and indigenous groups—from project benefits.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement country-adapted Stakeholder Engagement Plans, deploy inclusive Risk Communication and Community Engagement strategies, and establish functional Grievance Redress Mechanisms.
gen_risks.evidence: Potential social risks are substantial and relate to: (i) inadequate stakeholder engagement... (ii) the exclusion of vulnerable or disadvantaged groups...

gen_risks.description: The increased presence of project workers and health personnel in rural and conflict-affected communities creates substantial risks of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse and Sexual Harassment (SEA/SH).
gen_risks.mitigation: Prepare and enforce country-specific SEA/SH Action Plans, recruit dedicated GBV specialists, train all project workers, require signed codes of conduct, and establish GBV-sensitive grievance channels.
gen_risks.evidence: The overall project SEA/SH risks are judged to be substantial... increased presence of new health workforce... may create concerns of Sexual exploitation and abuse

gen_risks.description: Delays in executing required inter-agency MoUs (e.g., CEMAC-WOAH) or harmonizing cross-border data-sharing agreements and regulatory protocols could hamper regional disease surveillance and response.
gen_risks.mitigation: Convene the Regional Coordination Committee regularly, leverage CEMAC's political mandate to drive subregional alignment, and closely monitor MoU conditionality deadlines.
gen_risks.evidence: Prior to carrying out any relevant activity under Part 1.1... enter into a Memorandum of Understanding... with the WOAH

gen_risks.description: Expanded laboratory diagnostic testing and healthcare facility operations will generate hazardous chemical, biological, and medical waste, posing environmental contamination and health risks if improperly managed.
gen_risks.mitigation: Update and operationalize National Healthcare Waste Management Plans, supply proper biohazard management equipment, and train laboratory personnel in biosafety and biosecurity protocols.
gen_risks.evidence: laboratories will be supplied with reagents, chemicals, and equipment that may constitute medical waste once used.

gen_risks.description: Severe climate events such as flooding and extreme heat in Central Africa threaten health facility infrastructure, disrupt medical supply chains, and trigger climate-sensitive disease outbreaks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate EDGE green and resilient building standards, install solar power and flood-proofing in facility refurbishments, and integrate climate early warning alerts into surveillance systems.
gen_risks.evidence: Climate change contributed to at least 50 percent of natural disasters registered in Cameroon, CAR, Chad, and RoC between 1980 and 2020...

gen_risks.description: Weak institutional capacity and complex multi-sectoral coordination across human, animal, and environmental health ministries in five implementing entities may cause operational bottlenecks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish dedicated PIU structures with qualified technical and fiduciary specialists, deliver hands-on World Bank coaching, and operationalize National Steering Committees for One Health coordination.
gen_risks.evidence: gaps are primarily due to limited domestic and regional resources, weak institutional capacities and governance mechanisms, and insufficient multisectoral coordination.

gen_risks.description: Active armed conflict, insurgent attacks (e.g., Boko Haram), and civil unrest in FCV zones (such as CAR, Far-North/NW/SW Cameroon, and Chad borders) threaten worker safety and restrict access to project sites.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop and implement site-specific Security Risk Assessments and Security Management Plans, adopt flexible implementation arrangements, and coordinate closely with local community leaders.
gen_risks.evidence: Fragility in AFW is exacerbated by conflict and violence... Regional conflicts, such as Boko Haram attacks... can spread instability...

gen_risks.description: Sudden, large-scale influxes of refugees and internally displaced persons fleeing regional conflicts overwhelm local health services and accelerate cross-border disease transmission.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deploy targeted mobile surveillance and health service teams to border zones and refugee settlements, and utilize CERC financing for rapid emergency response reallocation if required.
gen_risks.evidence: Chad currently hosts over 1.5 million IDPs and refugees due to conflict in Lake Chad Basin and instability in Sudan, CAR, and Libya.

gt_risks.description: Political and governance risk (Moderate), considering fragility, socio-political instability, violence and weak governance of beneficiary countries.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close engagement by the World Bank to coordinate activities with other key partners.

gt_risks.description: Technical design risk (Substantial), considering the complexities of coordinating national-level and regional-level activities to align and build on each other, and the different levels of readiness at country-level.
gt_risks.mitigation: Exploring the possibility of a coordinated implementation arrangement with CEMAC as the lead technical coordination body for regional activities.

gt_risks.description: Weak institutional capacity for implementation and sustainability (Substantial), combined with overstretched or nonexistent PIUs in respective countries.
gt_risks.mitigation: Strengthening the existing PIUs and intensive capacity building and targeted TA for newly established PIUs.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risk (Substantial) due to weak governance structures and inadequate FM systems.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close implementation support by the World Bank, including TA as well as additional training and coaching on fiduciary processes.

gt_risks.description: E&S risk (Substantial) given the security risks associated with service delivery in FCV (fragility, conflict, and violence) settings.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close implementation support by the World Bank, including TA as well as additional training and coaching on managing E&S risks.
